note: Thought Sorter statements. keep=true accepts uncertainty or treats a thought as a thought. keep=false demands certainty, inflates threat, or is reassurance in disguise. No statement asserts a factual outcome. DRAFT: needs a clinician's review before public release.

items.text: I can carry on without being sure.
A thought is just a thought.
I don't need to feel certain to move on.
Doubt can come along while I keep going.
I read it once. That is enough for now.
I can leave a question unanswered.
Feeling unsure is uncomfortable, and I can stand it.
I locked up once. I'm walking away.
My mind is offering a what-if again.
I can notice a worry and not chase it.
I don't have to ask anyone about this.
A sensation can be there without an explanation.
I have to check until it feels right.
I must be completely sure before I move on.
If I thought it, it must mean something.
I need to read it again or I'll miss something.
I can't relax until someone tells me it's okay.
One more check and then I'll be certain.
Any doubt means something is wrong.
I must find out what this feeling means right now.
If I don't check, something terrible will happen.
I can't stand not knowing.
I have to get rid of this thought.
I should search online until I have an answer.
Maybe, maybe not. I'm getting on with my day.
The urge to check is loud. I can wait.
I understood enough of that page to continue.
I can send the message without reading it again.
Not knowing is part of ordinary life.
The worry is here. So is the washing-up.
I can feel anxious and still do the next thing.
I'll let this question stay open.
I don't need a second opinion from my friend tonight.
I noticed a sensation. I'm returning to what I was doing.
Thoughts come and go without my help.
I can leave the house with the doubt in my pocket.
A quick look won't hurt, just to be sure.
I should reread the email in case I said something wrong.
If I feel anxious, there must be a real danger.
I need to ask again, just to hear it once more.
I can't start anything else until this is settled.
Having this thought means I'm careless.
I should keep monitoring this feeling in my body.
If I'm not sure I did it, I probably didn't.
I must understand every word before turning the page.
It's irresponsible not to double-check.
I need to look this up before I can sleep.
The thought keeps coming back, so it must be important.
I may have made a mistake. I'm carrying on anyway.
I can't know for sure, and I don't need to.
The 'not right' feeling can ride along with me.
My memory of doing it is fuzzy. I'm leaving it there.
I'll finish the chapter without going back.
The what-if doesn't need an answer from me.
I can let the urge rise and fall by itself.
Asking again would feed the doubt. I'll sit with it.
I'm willing to not know how this turns out.
Sensations change all day. I don't need to track them.
I can do things well enough without doing them perfectly.
Anxiety is a feeling. I can have it and keep going.
If I check carefully once more, I can finally stop.
Other people are sure, so I should be too.
I'd never forgive myself if I skipped the check and was wrong.
I should replay it in my head until I remember clearly.
If I can't rule it out, I have to treat it as true.
I'll just ask in a different way so it doesn't count.
Reading it slowly three times is just being thorough.
A responsible person would make certain.
I need to compare how I feel now with yesterday.
If the thought upsets me this much, it must be a warning.
I should work out exactly why I had that thought.
I'll feel better once I've looked it up, so I should.
I'd like certainty. I can live without getting it.
It might be a mistake. I'm not going back to look.
The discomfort is the practice, not a problem to fix.
I'm choosing not to work this out right now.
The doubt will ask again. I can decline again.
I can leave a sentence half understood.
I don't need my partner to tell me what they think.
There might be a risk. I'm getting on with dinner.
I'll let my body do what it does without a report.
Feeling unsure about the door is allowed.
I can hold the thought lightly and keep typing.
Not checking feels wrong, and I'm doing it anyway.
I checked, so I know it's fine.
They said it's okay, so now I can relax.
I'll just take a photo so I don't have to wonder later.
I read online that it's nothing, so that's settled.
I'm sure it's fine. It's definitely fine.
If I go over it logically, I can prove there's no problem.
I'll check just this once, as a reward for waiting.
Nothing bad happened last time, so nothing will this time.
I'll reread only the important part.
I need to feel calm before I can carry on.
I'll keep an eye on it, just casually.
If I distract myself hard enough, the thought will go away.
I don't know, and I'm leaving it at that.
The thought may come back all day. I have things to do.
I can act on what matters while the alarm keeps ringing.
Maybe I missed something. I'm turning the page.
I'm not going to settle this in my head.
I can want an answer and not go looking.
The itch to confirm is here. I'm not scratching it.
I'll let today be uncertain.
I don't need to feel ready. I can start.
The worry gets a seat. It doesn't get the wheel.
I can end the conversation without one more 'are you sure?'
This might never feel finished. I'm stopping here.
I'm only asking because I want their honest opinion.
I'm not checking, I'm just walking past to see.
I've done my practice, so the thing I fear won't happen.
If I call it only a thought, then I know nothing is wrong.
Uncertainty is okay because the odds are tiny anyway.
I'll wait ten minutes, then I've earned a proper check.
I skimmed it again by accident, so I may as well reread it.
I just need to hear it from an expert once, then I'll stop.
I'll go back over the day in my head, only to be thorough.
Once the anxiety is gone, I'll know it was nothing.
I'm sure enough now, because I ran through it twice in my mind.
A quick search is different from really looking it up.
